author: Rdk123
text:
Hello mate,

Thank you for your reply the other day, and for your charts and progress today. Really appreciate it.

I really like the way you adapt to the market, this will be something I will hopefully be more in tune with over time. This seems to be where I am struggling at the minute as I think my brain is craving a common set of rules that can be applied. I'm really struggling with the flexibility required, when you say no two set ups are the same you are 100% right and I think this is where a lot of us fall down. We seem to be our own worst enemy's!

One thing I will ask about your style, is there a particular decision you like to trade from? As from the chart you posted, you must be on your toes watching and waiting for your conditions, I imagine considering and watching out for numerous different set ups would be very mentally tiring!

For me, I'm looking for the set up/ decision I'm most comfortable trading from and building the patience to wait for it with an eye on what is happening in the bigger picture.

You've been really helpful, I really appreciate it.

Robbie

author: pucci
text:
Hello Robbie,

All of the trades I take are either FTR setups or reverse FTRs. The latter is nothing but an ignored higher low or lower high. The trick here is to give the trades enough room to breath while it may go against you a bit, and more importantly to close out early. A lot of times my RR is not really a good one per RR rules. That's because I will mostly close at the first area of opposition. I have deleted from my system the notion of "Price will/should break" because we are coming from HTF SD or what have you. In the event it does break I will re-enter. It is indeed tiresome to be watching and micromanaging entries and exist. But the advantage is really no more than a couple of hours work per day. I often trade until London closes but that is not really necessary as most days I make my quota even before London opens. For example, today I made 12% in two hours. I could call it a day or maybe not, we'll see. Below is the P&L chart of this morning:

In the past year I must have sat in front of FT2 over 18hrs a day. Sometimes I'd get no sleep whatsoever. I must be thicker than all the rest on here cause there was always something I couldn't apply. Then it dawned on me to focus on one setup, and that's exactly what I did. Now I do recognize all the different ones as well, but I don't' necessarily trade them. I stick with my setup in thick and thin. Yes I do get stopped out like anyone else in this business but it usually is nothing more than a tiny scratch. As you mentioned, patience is the key. So is trading every one of your setups religiously, whether they get stopped out or not. I am in no way affiliated or trying to promote Michael Douglas' book Trading in the Zone, but it was a game changer for me. It might not have the same effect on everyone else. It benefited me greatly and this is why I am mentioning it again.

I hope I answered everything you meant to ask.

Have a great day,

Cheers,

BTW

text:
Thank you very much for your time,

I started reading through all of your analysis last night (it's taking some time to take in, you're very thorough), I really admire your dedication, it's obviously part of the reason you are so comfortable with what you trade now and it really does spur me on.

Everybody has their own drive to make them succeed and you very kindly mention your own personal life in your journal. I feel like this forum is all about give and take, so here's a bit of give from me.

I've been interested in trading for a few years now, never really jumping in, never really know what i was doing until I came across RTM last year. I got the bug, it was something I needed to figure out and like everyone on here I've had my ups and downs along the way, it's learning and in life.

In August 2013 my dad was diagnosed with terminal brain cancer, I was an traveling radio and satellite engineer, I immediately started the process of quitting my job to move back home to Durham (dragging my girlfriend with me). My dad has had his ups and downs but I've been here. The downs were more frequent last month so I had no hesitation about quitting my job to spend time with my dad and really nail down what has became a passion for trading so I can make a living from it.

I will most certainly be getting a copy of that book.

And if I can be bit cheeky and ask a favor, I've just posted a visual representation of what I'm seeing at the minute on my journal, I think it's a setup I'd like to really investigate and take hold of, you don't fancy giving it the

up of down do you? Just

in case what I've drawn is totally wrong and I start heading down the wrong path.

Cheers,

Robbie

author: antraxia
text:
pucci wrote: Hello Robbie,

All of the trades I take are either FTR setups or reverse FTRs. The latter is nothing but an ignored higher low or lower high. The trick here is to give the trades enough room to breath while it may go against you a bit, and more importantly to close out early. A lot of times my RR is not really a good one per RR rules. That's because I will mostly close at the first area of opposition. I have deleted from my system the notion of "Price will/should break" because we are coming from HTF SD or what have you. In the event it does break I will re-enter.

This has been my downfall up to this point as well! Looking at IF's charts can be misleading as I assume that price should do what I think it should especially when in HTF areas. He knows at least 1 thing that I don't (maximal retrace before the ITs will flip from long to short). Since I don't have that nailed down yet I now I assume I'm wrong and let the market prove me right.

Then it dawned on me to focus on one setup, and that's exactly what I did. Now I do recognize all the different ones as well, but I don't' necessarily trade them. I stick with my setup in thick and thin.

This is also awesome advice. I have been struggling to create a trading "method" and I'm so glad to see you mention this. I only need 1:2 a week for what I want to achieve. The math takes care of the rest. I find I have too many options and that I end up sitting on the sidelines wondering if the setup is good enough and then when I take them I get 1 R or a BE or a loss as I've watched all the 50:1 go by and am left with the dross. think sitting for 3 hours is the way to go as I won't miss setups. I now only traded DPs pretty much the same way as you do. There are super important DPs and others designed to trick people out of their money (those are probably your reverse FTRs). Both these usually provide a bounce.

The only thing I'm struggling with is the reverse R:R that you mentioned above. Sometimes my stop has to be 2 times my first target but it often works out. How did you overcome this mental challenge? Through rigorous practice? Its great to see you doing so well. Thanks for sharing with us. Cheers.

author: pucci
text:
antraxia wrote: The only thing I'm struggling with is the reverse R:R that you mentioned above. Sometimes my stop has to be 2 times my first target but it often works out. How did you overcome this mental challenge? Through rigorous practice? Its great to see you doing so well. Thanks for sharing with us. Cheers.

Hi John,

Well for me first and foremost is the preservation of capital. That said, I try my best to get out with something. There is a saying I was brought up with "Kleinvieh macht auch Mist" and I apply that to trading. I don't mind building my dream home one brick at a time (if you get what I mean). My way of looking at RR is definitely challenging, so was shifting my trading from what is mainstream to what we learn through SD and RTM. It's a mindset I guess, I got used to. Don't get me wrong, I often have trades that exceed any RR I would have put out for them to start with. I just don't expect that to happen when I enter. What I do expect is that anything can happen at any time in the market and I'm defending my capital at all costs.

Hope that helps
